TSA **did inhibit RPE activation-associated responses** in the in vitro PVR model.

- **Primary paper:** “Trichostatin A Inhibits Retinal Pigmented Epithelium Activation in an In Vitro Model of Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy,” *Journal of Ocular Pharmacology and Therapeutics* (2016), **PMID: 27494828**.
- **Model and treatment:** The study used ARPE-19 cells, primary porcine RPE, and induced-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived RPE. Cells were treated with TGFβ2 (10 ng/mL), with or without TSA (0.1 μM), a broad-spectrum histone deacetylase inhibitor.
- **Endpoints and reported results:** Collagen-matrix contraction and scratch-assay migration were reduced by TSA in the TGFβ2 model. TSA-treated wounded iPS-RPE monolayers also showed lower α-SMA. The abstract additionally reports reduced RPE proliferation.
- **Mechanism:** The study supports a role for acetylation/HDAC activity in RPE activation, but the retrieved evidence does not establish a more specific molecular mechanism.

Yes. In the in-vitro PVR model, trichostatin A (0.1 μM) reduced RPE activation-associated responses, including TGFβ2-induced collagen-matrix contraction and migration; the study also reported reduced proliferation and α-SMA in wounded iPS-derived RPE. The experiments included ARPE-19, primary porcine RPE, and iPS-derived RPE. This supports an inhibitory effect in vitro, not clinical efficacy. (2016; PMID: 27494828)
